_meta.indication: Topical treatment of acne vulgaris in patients 9 years of age and older

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, multicenter, parallel-group, double-blind, vehicle-controlled trial of 12 weeks
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects 9 years and older with moderate facial and truncal acne vulgaris
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints (face) at Week 12: success on IGA (clear/almost clear with ≥2-grade improvement), absolute change in facial inflammatory lesion count, and absolute change in facial noninflammatory lesion count
pivotal_trials.result: IGA success 29.4% vs 19.5% vehicle; facial inflammatory lesion change -19.0 vs -15.4; facial noninflammatory lesion change -25.0 vs -17.9; statistically superior to vehicle (p ≤ 0.001)

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, multicenter, parallel-group, double-blind, vehicle-controlled trial of 12 weeks (identical design to Study 1)
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects 9 years and older with moderate facial and truncal acne vulgaris
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints (face) at Week 12: success on IGA (clear/almost clear with ≥2-grade improvement), absolute change in facial inflammatory lesion count, and absolute change in facial noninflammatory lesion count
pivotal_trials.result: IGA success 42.3% vs 25.7% vehicle; facial inflammatory lesion change -24.2 vs -18.7; facial noninflammatory lesion change -30.1 vs -21.6; statistically superior to vehicle (p ≤ 0.001)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥1%) were application site irritation (7.5% vs 0.3% vehicle), application site pruritus (2.4% vs 0.8%), and sunburn (2.6% vs 0.5%). Skin irritation (erythema, scaling, dryness, stinging/burning) may occur, typically peaking within the first 4 weeks. No deaths or drug-related serious adverse events in the Phase 3 trials.
target_moa: Trifarotene is a retinoid that is an agonist of retinoic acid receptors (RARs), with particular potency at the RAR-gamma subtype (EC50 ~7.6 nM), which modulates target genes involved in cell differentiation and inflammation

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to an advisory committee; the application did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues unexpected for a drug of this class

summary.text: Standard review NDA 211527 submitted under the 505(b)(1) pathway for a new molecular entity; received October 4, 2018 with a PDUFA goal date of October 4, 2019 and standard review classification; approved based on two adequate and well-controlled Phase 3 trials without accelerated approval.

Galderma Research and Development, Inc. submitted a new drug application (NDA) 211527 for AKLIEF (trifarotene) Cream, 0.005% for the treatment of acne vulgaris under the 505(b)(1) regulatory pathway. Acne vulgaris is a common, chronic dermatological disorder of sebaceous follicles which primarily affects adolescents and young adults. AKLIEF is a new molecular entity.
